body.statement:
The asserted whole-array uniform selector-conditional convergence is false under \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), and its failure can be maximal even inside the stationary independent-over-time square subclass satisfying Shi et al.'s Assumptions 1--5, supplementary conditions D.1--D.10, and the fixed-role full-rank condition for both predeclared roles.  Specifically, fix
\[
 0<\kappa<\frac{6373}{15369},\qquad
 0<\nu<\frac{39}{625},
\]
and a sufficiently large finite moment envelope.  For every sufficiently large integer \(q\), there is a whole triangular array \((P_j^{(q)})_{j\geq1}\in\mathcal M(0)\) with constant treatment effect \(\Delta_t=\tau\), conditionally independent factor-measurement errors, and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{39}{625},\qquad
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=V_s=1\quad(s\in\mathcal S),
\]
whose stacked limiting covariance is singular, but for
\[
 T_q=
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
      {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}
\]
one has
\[
 \lim_{q\to\infty}
 \mathbb E_{P_q^{(q)}}\!\left[
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
  \left|
   \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}\{T_q\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A\}-\Phi(x)
  \right|
 \right]=1.
\]
Thus positive limiting marginal variances, coordinatewise studentization, a logarithm-squared mixing gap, and singular-covariance-safe Gaussian mapping do not yield whole-array uniform inference without a uniform finite-row variance and distributional-stabilization condition.
body.proof_tex:
We construct a sequence of whole triangular arrays and verify every asserted property.  Put
\[
 B_0=\frac{6373}{30000},\qquad
 x_0=\frac18,\qquad
 \bar b_0=\frac78,\qquad
 t_0=\frac{5123}{10000},\qquad
 c_0=t_0^{-1/2}.
\]
Direct calculation gives
\[
 t_0+B_0+x_0=4B_0,
 \qquad \eta_0=\frac{B_0}{t_0+B_0+x_0}=\frac14,
 \qquad \frac{B_0}{t_0}=\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa.
\]
For row index \(j\), set \(m_j=j\).  Hence \(j/m_j=1\), so \(r=1\) by \(\texttt{ass:sample-ratio}\).

Fix a sufficiently large integer \(q\).  We define a whole array \(P_\bullet^{(q)}=(P_j^{(q)})_{j\geq1}\).  Every row is independent and identically distributed over the two-sided time index.  In each ordinary row \(j\ne q\), generate mutually independent variables
\[
 F_t\sim N(0,B_0),\qquad
 e_{1t},e_{2t}\sim N(0,x_0),\qquad
 \varepsilon_{0t}\sim N(0,\bar b_0),
\]
and set
\[
 Y_t(0)=F_t+\varepsilon_{0t},\qquad
 \Delta_t=\tau,qquad
 W_{1t}=c_0(F_t+e_{1t}),\qquad
 W_{2t}=c_0(F_t+e_{2t}).
\]
Role one uses \(W_1\) as donor and \(W_2\) as proxy, and role two exchanges them.  The Gaussian variable \(\varepsilon_{0t}\) may equivalently be written as the sum of two independent \(N(0,7/16)\) variables, so the ordinary rows have the Gaussian factor form covered by \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\).

In the exceptional row \(j=q\), retain \(F_t\sim N(0,B_0)\), put
\[
 p_q=q^{-2},\qquad a_q=q^{-4},
\]
generate mutually independent variables
\[
 I_{q,t}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_q),qquad
 Z_{0t},Z_{1t},Z_{2t}\sim N(0,1),
\]
and define
\[
 \varepsilon_{0t}=I_{q,t}-p_q+a_qZ_{0t},
 \qquad e_{1t}=a_qZ_{1t},
 \qquad e_{2t}=a_qZ_{2t}.
\]
Use the same displayed definitions of \(Y_t(0)\), \(\Delta_t\), \(W_{1t}\), and \(W_{2t}\).  Thus the exceptional centered jump occurs in the treated unit's idiosyncratic untreated-outcome error, while treatment is constant.  Conditional on \(F_t\), that error and the two donor measurement errors are mutually independent.  In every row,
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_j^{(q)}}\Delta_t=\tau,
\]
so the causal target is the stationary mean treatment effect, independently of the observed bridge identity established below.

We next prove that \(P_\bullet^{(q)}\in\mathcal M(0)\).  Independence over time implies strict stationarity and gives absolute-regularity coefficients \(\beta_j(h)=0\) for every \(h\geq1\), verifying \(\texttt{ass:stationarity}\) and \(\texttt{ass:geometric-beta-mixing}\).  All Gaussian variances and loadings are bounded uniformly in \(j\) and \(q\), while \(0\leq I_{q,t}\leq1\) and \(0<a_q,p_q\leq1\).  Hence, for the fixed \(\delta_0>0\),
\[
 \sup_q\sup_j
 \mathbb E_{P_j^{(q)}}\lVert X_t\rVert^{8+\delta_0}<\infty.
\]
Taking \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) above this finite quantity verifies \(\texttt{ass:moment-bound}\).

For either role, every row has
\[
 M_s=\mathbb E(Z_{s,t}W_{D_s,t})=c_0^2B_0
     =\frac{B_0}{t_0}=\frac{6373}{15369}>\kappa
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E\{Z_{s,t}Y_t(0)\}=c_0B_0=M_s/c_0.
\]
Thus \(M_s\) is invertible with the required rank margin, and the definition of \(\alpha_s\) yields
\[
 \alpha_s=\frac1{c_0},
 \qquad
 Y_t(0)-W_{D_s,t}\alpha_s=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{s,t},
\]
where \(e_{s,t}\) is the measurement error of the donor used by role \(s\).  Both terms on the right are centered.  This proves \(\texttt{ass:bridge-rank}\) and \(\texttt{ass:bridge-centering}\).  It also proves, rather than defines, the observed-law identification equation
\[
 \mathbb E\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{D_s,t}\alpha_s\}=\tau,
\]
which links the bridge residual mean to the separately defined causal target.

Within each row, \(W_1\) and \(W_2\) have the same distribution and the same joint second moments with \(Y_t(0)\).  Therefore their population ridge coefficients and minimized population ridge losses coincide:
\[
 L_{1,j}=L_{2,j}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sup_{j\geq1}\sqrt j\,|L_{1,j}-L_{2,j}|=0,
\]
which is \(\texttt{ass:bounded-selector-gap-array}\) with \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}=0\).

It remains to verify the limiting covariance and its margins.  Since \(\mathbb E W_{D_s,t}=0\), the definition \(H_s=-\mu_s'M_s^{-1}\) gives \(H_s=0\), and hence
\[
 \psi_{s,t}=0,qquad A_s=0
\]
for both roles.  All rows after index \(q\) have the same ordinary Gaussian law.  Their centered six-dimensional score vector is a degree-two polynomial in a fixed-dimensional Gaussian vector, and therefore has finite moments of every order.  The ordinary-row long-run covariance is just its one-period covariance because observations are independent over time.  It follows that the rowwise long-run covariance matrices are constant for all \(j>q\) and converge to a finite positive-semidefinite matrix, proving \(\texttt{ass:covariance-limit}\).  The limiting stacked covariance is singular because its two pre-ATT coordinates \(A_1,A_2\) vanish identically.  No covariance inversion is used here.

For completeness, the asserted Gaussian coordinates also exist even with this singular covariance.  If \(G_t\) is the ordinary-row centered score vector with covariance \(\Sigma_G\), then, for every fixed vector \(u\), its finite third moment and Taylor's theorem give
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\!\left(\frac{\mathrm i u'G_t}{\sqrt j}\right)
 =1-\frac{u'\Sigma_Gu}{2j}+O(j^{-3/2}).
\]
Independence over \(t\) implies that the characteristic function of \(j^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^jG_t\) is the \(j\)-th power of the last display and hence converges to
\[
 \exp\!\left(-\frac12u'\Sigma_Gu\right).
\]
The Cramér--Wold device therefore gives the possibly singular joint Gaussian limit used to define \(D,A_s,R_s\).

We derive the exact selector variance directly from the ridge criterion.  In an ordinary row,
\[
 \mathbb E W_{jt}^2=c_0^2(B_0+x_0),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\{W_{jt}Y_t(0)\}=c_0B_0.
\]
Therefore the scalar population ridge coefficient is
\[
 a_j=\frac{c_0B_0}{1+c_0^2(B_0+x_0)}
     =\frac{B_0\sqrt{t_0}}{t_0+B_0+x_0},
\]
and its fitted value is
\[
 W_{jt}a_j=\eta_0(F_t+e_{jt}).
\]
The two roles have the same coefficient norm, so their penalty contributions cancel in the one-period loss contrast.  On putting
\[
 U_t=(1-\eta_0)F_t+\varepsilon_{0t},
\]
we obtain the exact identity
\[
 \ell_{1,t}-\ell_{2,t}
 =-2\eta_0U_t(e_{1t}-e_{2t})
   +\eta_0^2(e_{1t}^2-e_{2t}^2).
\]
Here \(U_t\) is independent of \((e_{1t},e_{2t})\), is centered, and has variance \((1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0\).  The two displayed summands are uncorrelated because the donor errors are independent centered Gaussian variables and hence have zero third moments.  Also
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(e_{1t}-e_{2t})=2x_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(e_{1t}^2-e_{2t}^2)=4x_0^2.
\]
Since observations are independent over time, the long-run variance of the loss contrast, which is \(\operatorname{Var}(D)\), is consequently
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(D)
 &=4\eta_0^2\{(1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0\}(2x_0)
   +4\eta_0^4x_0^2. 
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed,
\[
 (1-\eta_0)^2B_0+\bar b_0
 =\frac{159119}{160000},
\]
and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)
 =\frac{159119}{2560000}+\frac1{4096}
 =\frac{159744}{2560000}
 =\frac{39}{625}>\nu.
\]
This proves \(\texttt{ass:selector-variance-margin}\).  In an ordinary row the post residuals are
\[
 v_{1,t}=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{1t},
 \qquad
 v_{2,t}=\varepsilon_{0t}-e_{2t},
\]
so independence gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(R_s)=\bar b_0+x_0=1.
\]
Together with \(A_s=0\) and \(r=1\), this yields
\[
 V_s=\operatorname{Var}(A_s)+r\operatorname{Var}(R_s)=1>\nu.
\]
Thus \(\texttt{ass:att-variance-margin}\) holds, and \(\texttt{lem:gap-variance-inheritance}\) gives
\[
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=V_s=1
\]
because \(\operatorname{Var}(A_s)=0\).  We have now verified every member condition of \(\texttt{def:panel-class}\), so \(P_\bullet^{(q)}\in\mathcal M(0)\).  Moreover, \(\texttt{prop:shi-anchor-transfer}\) applies row by row: the bridge is square and full rank, treatment is constant, the factor-measurement errors are conditionally independent, and the exceptional treated error is a centered rare jump convolved with a nondegenerate Gaussian.  Thus these witness laws lie in the stated common subclass; this uses no claim that the complete reduced-form and published classes contain one another.

We finally analyze the estimator in the diagonal row \(j=q\).  Let \(\mathcal N_q\) be the event that \(I_{q,t}=0\) at every time in the late bridge-fitting block \(\mathcal B_q\) and the post block \(\mathcal C_q\).  Those blocks are disjoint from the early selection block and together contain at most \(2q\) observations.  Independence over time therefore gives independence of \(\mathcal N_q\) and \(\mathcal F_A\), as well as
\[
 \Pr(\mathcal N_q)
 \geq(1-p_q)^{2q}
 =(1-q^{-2})^{2q}\longrightarrow1.
\]
The label \(\widehat J_A\) is \(\mathcal F_A\)-measurable.  We derive bounds uniformly over its two possible values.

Fix either selected role, let \(j\in\{1,2\}\) denote its donor, and let \(k\ne j\) denote its proxy.  On \(\mathcal N_q\), the true bridge residual on both retained blocks equals
\[
 r_{j,t}^0
 :=Y_t(0)-W_{jt}\alpha_j
 =-p_q+a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt}).
\]
Write a bar for an empirical average over \(\mathcal B_q\), and define
\[
 \widehat M_{j,q}
 =|\mathcal B_q|^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal B_q}W_{kt}W_{jt}.
\]
The scalar sample bridge equation gives the exact identity, whenever \(\widehat M_{j,q}\ne0\),
\[
 \widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j
 =\widehat M_{j,q}^{-1}|\mathcal B_q|^{-1}
   \sum_{t\in\mathcal B_q}W_{kt}r_{j,t}^0.
\]
The continuous Gaussian component makes \(\widehat M_{j,q}=0\) a null event.  Since \(|\mathcal B_q|/q\to1-\varrho>0\), the independent Gaussian factor observations and Chebyshev's inequality imply
\[
 \widehat M_{j,q}=c_0^2B_0+O_P(q^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \overline W_{k,\mathcal B_q}=O_P(q^{-1/2}).
\]
Conditional on \(\mathcal N_q\), the centered part of \(W_{kt}r_{j,t}^0\) has standard deviation \(O(a_q)\), while its constant-residual part is \(-p_qW_{kt}\).  The preceding identity consequently yields
\[
 \widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j
 =O_P\!\left(\frac{p_q+a_q}{\sqrt q}\right),
\]
uniformly over \(j=1,2\).  Similarly,
\[
 \overline W_{j,\mathcal C_q}=O_P(q^{-1/2}).
\]
Using the construction of \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}\), we therefore obtain on \(\mathcal N_q\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau
 &=\overline r^0_{j,\mathcal C_q}
   -(\widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j)\overline W_{j,\mathcal C_q}\\
 &=-p_q+O_P(a_qq^{-1/2})
   +O_P\{(p_q+a_q)q^{-1}\}\\
 &=-p_q\{1+o_P(1)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

We now bound the actual studentizing denominator.  For centered scalar observations \(g_1,\ldots,g_N\), the Bartlett estimator with bandwidth \(h\) and weights bounded by one satisfies
\[
 0\leq\widehat\Omega_g
 \leq(2h+1)N^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^Ng_t^2.
\]
This follows by expanding the lag-covariance sum and applying \(2|g_tg_{t-h}|\leq g_t^2+g_{t-h}^2\) at each lag.  The centered fitted post residual differs from \(a_q(Z_{0t}-Z_{jt})\) only by the centered version of \(-(\widehat\alpha_j-\alpha_j)W_{jt}\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{v,j}
 =O_P\!\left[
 h_q\left\{a_q^2+\frac{(p_q+a_q)^2}{q}\right\}
 \right].
\]
The fitted bridge sensitivity is the fitted analogue of \(-\mu_j'M_j^{-1}\).  Its donor-mean factor is estimated from a retained block and is \(O_P(q^{-1/2})\), while its fitted inverse moment is \(O_P(1)\); therefore
\[
 \widehat H_j=O_P(q^{-1/2}).
\]
Before multiplication by \(\widehat H_j\), the fitted bridge score has conditional second moment \(O_P(p_q^2+a_q^2)\).  Applying the same Bartlett inequality gives
\[
 \widehat\Omega_{\psi,j}
 =O_P\!\left\{\frac{h_q(p_q^2+a_q^2)}q\right\}.
\]
Because \(|\mathcal B_q|\asymp q\), \(m_q=q\), \(h_q=O(q^{1/5})\), and \(a_q\leq p_q\), the definition of the selected standard error implies
\[
 \widehat{\operatorname{se}}_j^2
 =O_P\!\left\{
 \frac{h_qa_q^2}{q}+\frac{h_qp_q^2}{q^2}
 \right\}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \frac{\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_j}{p_q}
 =O_P\!\left[
 \left\{
 \frac{h_qa_q^2}{qp_q^2}+\frac{h_q}{q^2}
 \right\}^{1/2}
 \right]=o_P(1),
\]
where the last equality uses \(p_q=q^{-2}\), \(a_q=q^{-4}\), and \(h_q=O(q^{1/5})\).  Since \(a_q>0\), the fitted post residual vector has a nonconstant continuous Gaussian component almost surely.  The finite-sample Bartlett kernel is positive definite on a nonzero centered residual vector when \(h_q<m_q\).  Thus \(\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_j>0\) almost surely for all sufficiently large \(q\).  Combining numerator and denominator bounds proves, on \(\mathcal N_q\),
\[
 T_q=
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
      {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}
 \longrightarrow-\infty
\]
in probability, uniformly over both early-selected labels.  Since \(\Pr(\mathcal N_q)\to1\), the same divergence holds unconditionally.

Choose a deterministic sequence \(b_q\to\infty\) slowly enough that
\[
 \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}(T_q>-b_q)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Let
\[
 K_q=
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
 \left|
  \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}(T_q\leq x\mid\mathcal F_A)-\Phi(x)
 \right|.
\]
Evaluation at the deterministic point \(-b_q\) and Jensen's inequality yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{P_q^{(q)}}K_q
 &\geq
 \mathbb E_{P_q^{(q)}}\left|
  \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}(T_q\leq-b_q\mid\mathcal F_A)-\Phi(-b_q)
 \right|\\
 &\geq
 \left|
  \Pr_{P_q^{(q)}}(T_q\leq-b_q)-\Phi(-b_q)
 \right|\longrightarrow1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Every Kolmogorov distance is at most one, so the matching upper bound is automatic and \(\mathbb E_{P_q^{(q)}}K_q\to1\).  This proves the asserted maximal whole-array failure.
body.justification: The diagonal counterexample identifies the exact whole-array quantifier failure and sharpens the conditional Gaussian-approximation error to its maximal possible value.
body.gap: Pointwise covariance limits and limiting variance margins do not control the finite row at which a supremum over whole arrays is evaluated.
body.consumer: Any valid uniformly justified split-sample redesign must add explicit uniform finite-row variance and distributional-stabilization conditions.
